subject: Heliosys renewal — executive sign-off requested for resilience package & SLA uplift
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal_team <legal@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-16T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Heliosys renewal — executive sign-off requested for resilience package & SLA uplift

Team,

Quick summary: Heliosys (annual spend ~ $980k) is up for renewal on 2026-06-15. They experienced a high-profile outage in April that impacted customer deliverables and prompted a procurement review; procurement is threatening to consolidate onto a competitor unless we offer meaningful remediation and price relief. Vivek has the relationship — they want price + SLA + term concessions.

What I'm asking for: an exec sign-off on a one-time retention package we can offer immediately to lock the renewal:
- One-time first-year discount: 25% off list for Year 1
- Credit: $50,000 operational credit to offset April impact (applied to first invoice)
- SLA uplift: bump to a 99.95% platform SLA for the renewal term, with a 15% service credit for any monthly breach (legal to review wording)
- Term reset: 12-month minimum commitment starting at signed renewal date (they requested flexibility on commit length)
- Optional: Resilience add-on ($15k/yr) for prioritized support and on-call escalation during major incidents

Attachments: proposal-heliosys-resilience-050626.pdf (offer markup) and heliosys-redlines-legal.docx (their redline requests).

Why approve: this is a high strategic account, retention preserves revenue and references in the vertical. Trade-offs: discount + credit will compress Yr1 revenue but we avoid churn and expansion risk across their enterprise.

Need by: COB 2026-05-20 so we can present a clean, signed offer before their procurement window closes.

Ask: Lauren — can we get authority to offer the package above (25% + $50k credit + SLA uplift + optional $15k resilience add-on)? If not, what ceilings should we set? Legal — please prioritize SLA and data-export redline review. Finance — confirm impact to Q2.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0128

---
Attachments: proposal-heliosys-resilience-050626.pdf; heliosys-redlines-legal.docx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal_team <legal@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-16T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Heliosys renewal — executive sign-off requested for resilience package & SLA uplift

Irene — thanks for the concise brief. I ran the ask by the account and they pushed back: they want deeper near-term relief given the outage impact. My recommendation to balance retention economics and precedent:
- Approve up to 20% first-year discount (we should aim lower than 25% unless Lauren signs off on the full concession)
- Consider a structured credit: $50k guaranteed + an additional $25k conditional credit if they sign within 7 days of offer
- Approve SLA uplift but require legal to narrow the credit language (cap exposure to 3 months of credits where feasible)
- Negotiate to secure an 18-month commitment (helps mitigate revenue hit) instead of just 12 months

Also propose we offer the resilience add-on as a paid item at $15k/yr and include a 90-day onboarding play from CSM. If Lauren OKs, I'll take this to Procurement and try to trade term length and the conditional $25k for the extra discount they want.

If we push to 25% + $75k credit they will likely sign same-day, but that sets a high discount precedent for the region.

Vivek
SVP, Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---
Note: I flagged heliosys-redlines-legal.docx for legal review (they've asked for broader audit log retention and self-service export).

From: Asha Ramesh <asha@heliosys.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-17T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Heliosys renewal — response and counter

Irene / Vivek — thanks for the proposal and for prioritizing this. I want to be clear about Heliosys' position so we can move quickly:
- We are prepared to renew but need meaningful remediation for April. We are asking for a 30% concession on Year 1 pricing plus a $75k operational credit.
- The SLA uplift is critical; we'll accept 99.95% but require specific language around incident communication, RCAs within 5 business days, and a defined credit ladder for severity 1 and 2 incidents.
- We also need a narrow data-export guarantee (48-hour export window) and audit log retention for 24 months.

If Redwood can confirm 30% + $75k + SLA drafting that matches our expectations we can commit to an 18-month renewal and expedite signatures. I have attached a signed redline for your review (heliosys-signed-redline.pdf).

Asha Ramesh
Director, Vendor Management | Heliosys Inc.
procure@heliosys.com

---
Attachments: heliosys-signed-redline.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, legal_team <legal@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Heliosys renewal — executive sign-off requested (please review & approve)

Lauren — forwarding the thread and their counter. Short ask for clarity: do we have authority to agree to 30% + $75k? Or is the floor 25% + $50k? They are offering an 18-month commitment if we meet their full ask, which offsets some of the revenue impact.

Key points for consideration (recommended trade-offs):
- Approve up to 25% + $50k now to avoid setting an outsized precedent. If you approve 25% + $50k, I will push for the 18-month commitment and the resilience add-on as a paid item.
- If you approve up to 30% + $75k, we should require a recoverable clause: e.g., true-up if they expand within 12 months (partial offset) or an agreed reference case/marketing commitment.
- Legal must sign SLA language that caps exposure (e.g., limit aggregate credit liability).

Deadline: procurement expects an answer by 2026-05-20 COB to make the June renewal window.

Please reply with authoritative guidance — need an OK/No and any guardrails.

Thanks,
Irene

> On May 17, 2026, Asha Ramesh <asha@heliosys.com> wrote:
> > We are prepared to renew but need meaningful remediation for April...

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, legal_team <legal@redwood.ai>, finance_team <finance@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-19T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Heliosys renewal — executive sign-off requested (please review & approve)

Irene — thank you for the concise packet and for mapping trade-offs. I approve the following, with conditions:

1) One-time concession: up to 25% discount on Year 1 list pricing and a $50k operational credit.
2) Term: require an 18-month committed term (not 12) in exchange for the concession; add a standard expansion true-up clause for any material expansion in first 12 months.
3) SLA uplift: legal to draft the 99.95% SLA language. Approve subject to legal capping total credit exposure to no more than 3 months of gross margin impact; legal & finance must sign off on final wording before signature.
4) Resilience add-on: approve offering at $15k/yr; do not provide as free concession. Include a 90-day CSM onboarding deliverable.

If Vivek can get procurement to accept the 25% + $50k + 18-month commit, we will sign. If they insist on 30% + $75k, escalate back to me with rationale for the additional delta (I may approve in narrow circumstances but need finance modelling first).

Lauren Bishop
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

---
Cc: finance_team for impact analysis; legal_team for SLA and data/export wording.
